attributes.name: Set of Common Divisors of Two Integers (Number Theory)
attributes.description: An integer c is a common divisor of two integers x and y iff c divides gcd(x, y). Therefore, the set of ALL common divisors of x and y is the complete set of all positive and negative divisors of gcd(x, y) = g (never containing 0, and containing every divisor d of g along with -d).
constraints: 0 is NEVER a divisor of any integer (any set containing 0 is invalid)

If 6 is in the set of all common divisors, then gcd(x, y) is a multiple of 6, so EVERY divisor of 6 ({-6, -3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3, 6}) MUST be in the set; a set like {-6, -2, -1, 1, 2, 6} that omits 3 and -3 is IMPOSSIBLE.

attributes.name: Common Divisor Transitivity & Closure Law
attributes.equation: CommonDivisors(x, y) = Divisors(gcd(x, y)) = {d in Z \ {0} : d | gcd(x, y)}. If 6 in S, then +-1, +-2, +-3, +-6 in S -> {-6, -3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3, 6}.

attributes.name: Logistic Population Growth & Carrying Capacity Control (Ecology)
attributes.description: In logistic population dynamics dN/dt = r*N*(1 - N/K), rapidly reproducing r-selected pest species (such as mosquitoes) quickly rebound from temporary mortality spikes back to the environment's carrying capacity K. The most effective long-term means of controlling the population is to reduce the carrying capacity K of the environment (e.g., eliminating standing water breeding sites) to lower the K value.
constraints: Reducing the carrying capacity (K) of the environment permanently lowers the equilibrium ceiling K
Increasing mortality rate alone causes temporary reduction followed by rapid exponential recovery when N < K

attributes.name: Verhulst Logistic Population Equation
attributes.equation: dN/dt = r * N * (1 - N / K); equilibrium population N* = K (reduce K to permanently lower population).

attributes.name: Quantum Efficiency & Binomial Photon Counting Statistics (Quantum Optics)
attributes.description: When N independent photons are incident on a detector with quantum efficiency eta (probability p = eta of detecting each photon), the number of detected photons follows a binomial distribution B(N, eta) with mean mu = N * eta and rms deviation (standard deviation) sigma = sqrt(N * eta * (1 - eta)).
constraints: For N = 100 photons and quantum efficiency eta = 0.1: mean = 100 * 0.1 = 10 detections
rms deviation = sqrt(100 * 0.1 * 0.9) = sqrt(9) = 3 (an average of 10 times, with an rms deviation of about 3)

attributes.name: Binomial Detector Mean and RMS Deviation
attributes.equation: mean = N * p = 100 * 0.1 = 10; rms_deviation = sqrt(N * p * (1 - p)) = sqrt(100 * 0.1 * 0.9) = 3.

attributes.name: Thin-Film Interference with Single Phase Inversion (Optics)
attributes.description: When light in air (n_air = 1.00) reflects normally off a thin film of oil (n_film = 1.50, thickness d = 500 nm) floating on water (n_water = 1.33), reflection at the top air->oil interface (n1 < n2) undergoes a 180-degree (pi, lambda/2) phase shift, while reflection at the bottom oil->water interface (n2 > n3, 1.50 > 1.33) has NO phase shift. Constructive interference (strongest reflection) therefore satisfies 2 * n_film * d = (m + 1/2) * lambda_air.
constraints: Since n_air (1.0) < n_oil (1.5) > n_water (1.33), only ONE reflection inverts phase
Constructive reflection condition: lambda_air = 2 * n_oil * d / (m + 0.5) = 1500 nm / (m + 0.5)
For m = 0: 3000 nm; m = 1: 1500 / 1.5 = 1000 nm; m = 2: 1500 / 2.5 = 600 nm (visible!). Thus 600 nm is most strongly reflected.

attributes.name: Single-Inversion Thin-Film Constructive Interference
attributes.equation: 2 * n_film * d = (m + 1/2) * lambda_air => for n=1.5, d=500 nm, m=2: lambda_air = 1500 / 2.5 = 600 nm.

attributes.name: Point Reflection of a Circle in the Plane (Analytic Geometry)
attributes.description: Reflecting every point (x, y) of a circle (x - x0)^2 + (y - y0)^2 = r^2 across a point P = (p, q) maps (x, y) -> (x', y') = (2p - x, 2q - y), which maps the center (x0, y0) to (2p - x0, 2q - y0) while preserving radius r.
constraints: For x^2 + y^2 = 16 reflected across (3, 2): new center is (6, 4) with r^2 = 16

attributes.name: Strict Profit / Earning Money Threshold vs. Break-Even Point (Quantitative Economics)
attributes.description: Break-even occurs at n_0 = FixedCost / (AnnualRevenue - AnnualCost) where net profit is $0. To START EARNING MONEY (strictly positive net profit > 0) when cashflows occur in discrete years, the required number of years is floor(n_0) + 1 = int(FixedCost // NetAnnualGain) + 1.
constraints: At break-even (Revenue == Cost), cumulative net profit is 0 (not yet earning money)
To start earning money (Revenue > Cost), if FixedCost / NetAnnualGain is an exact integer k (e.g., $90 / $7.50 = 12 years to break even), the person starts earning money in year k + 1 = 13.

attributes.name: Discrete Year Strict Profit Inequality
attributes.equation: NetProfit(n) = n * (Rev - Cost) - InitialCost > 0 <=> n > InitialCost / (Rev - Cost) => n_min = floor(InitialCost / (Rev - Cost)) + 1.

attributes.name: RegreSSHion OpenSSH Signal Handler Race Condition
attributes.description: A signal handler race condition in OpenSSH's server (sshd) on glibc-based Linux systems allows unauthenticated remote code execution as root when LoginGraceTime expires.

attributes.name: Veeam Backup & Replication Unauthenticated Deserialization RCE
attributes.description: Deserialization of untrusted data in Veeam Backup & Replication (12.0.0.1420 through 12.1.2.172) allows unauthenticated remote code execution via Backup.MountService on TCP port 6170.

attributes.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
attributes.description: The program executes concurrent code paths that access a shared resource without proper synchronization.
mitigations: Use atomic operations and reentrant-safe functions in signal handlers
Eliminate non-async-signal-safe calls such as syslog()/malloc()/free() inside SIGALRM handlers

attributes.name: Signal Handler Race Condition
attributes.description: A race condition occurs inside a signal handler that invokes non-reentrant or non-async-signal-safe functions.

attributes.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
attributes.description: The application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid and safe.
mitigations: Use safe serialization formats like JSON with strict schema validation
Enforce cryptographic signing and type allowlisting before deserializing

attributes.name: Leveraging Time-of-Check and Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) Race Conditions
attributes.description: An adversary exploits a race window between checking a resource state and using it.

attributes.name: Object Injection
attributes.description: An adversary crafts serialized objects containing gadget chains to execute arbitrary code during deserialization.

attributes.name: Payments Database Region A/B Failover Postmortem #209
attributes.description: At 02:14 UTC on 3 June, the Region A payments primary database halted when write-ahead logs filled 100% of the 500 GB volume. Automated failover promoted the Region B replica at 02:31 UTC (17 minutes elapsed). 1,820 transactions were delayed and 14 transactions failed permanently. The volume was expanded to 1 TB with an 80% alert threshold.
constraints: Outage start: 02:14 UTC
Failover complete: 02:31 UTC (17 minutes elapsed)
Delayed: 1,820 transactions
Failed permanently: 14 transactions
New disk size: 1 TB (80% alert)

attributes.name: Aurora Distributed Storage v4.2 Specification
attributes.description: The primary metadata cluster runs on PostgreSQL 16 across 3 availability zones with synchronous WAL replication. Read replicas refresh within 12 ms P99 latency, cold archival snapshots export every 6 hours, and the Kotlin coordinator enforces a maximum batch size of 4,096 records per transaction.
constraints: Database: PostgreSQL 16
Coordinator language: Kotlin
Max batch size: 4,096 records per transaction
Replica P99 latency: 12 ms
